## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain secured their spot as the 2025-26 winner by defeating Arsenal on penalties in the final, ending a 1-1 draw with a 4-3 scoreline. Their path was defined by elite offensive metrics and defensive solidity. They generated an average of 62.6 attacks per game, ranking at the 97th percentile among that season's teams. Possession was dominant at 64.0%, while they completed 671 passes per game, a perfect 100th percentile figure locally. Defensively, they were equally formidable, allowing just 6.9 opponent shots per game and 3.0 on target, placing them in the bottom 12% of teams for shots conceded.

## Would the model have picked them?
The predictive model would likely have selected Paris Saint-Germain as a strong contender. Although the base rate suggests only an 8.3% chance for any random knockout team to reach the final, the model assigned this club a 16.1% probability of success. This placed them at rank 4 among all 24 teams in the season's knockout stages. The algorithm calculated an expected knockout stage value of 1.73, indicating a trajectory well beyond the quarter-finals and closer to the semi-finals or final. While the model was trained on historical data from other seasons rather than this specific campaign, its high probability score suggests it would have identified them as a top-tier finalist candidate based on their underlying performance metrics.

## Weak spots
Despite their success, several statistical areas dragged down the model's confidence. The most significant negative factor was long passes, which accounted for only 8.6% of their total passes, ranking at the 5th percentile historically and contributing -0.22 to their stage expectation. Surprisingly, a high volume of shots per game (14.9) also negatively impacted the prediction by -0.13, despite being a top-tier offensive stat. Additionally, they covered only 114.5 km per game, a figure that ranked at the 28th percentile for their season and contributed +0.10 to the model's expectation, yet the low distance metric was flagged as a weakness in the broader analysis.

Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events or numbers that are not in the facts. Percentiles compare a team with other Champions League teams: 90 means higher than 90% of them. For stats marked '(lower is better)', a LOW percentile is good. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: +0.30 means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by 0.30 of a round. Write plain markdown without tables.
